subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@fintechlabs.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful. Quick summary of our needs so we have it written down and to confirm next steps: 

- Deployment mode: prefer Dedicated capacity (customer-managed data isolation). We may evaluate Private VPC later but want to start with Dedicated.
- Security: SOC2 controls are required; procurement will need a checklist (I can share one).
- Traffic: estimate peak ~200-300 TPS for text generation endpoints, sustained ~120 TPS.
- Concurrency: target ~40-60 concurrent requests on peak.
- Token mix: average prompt tokens ~40, average generated tokens ~160. We also run embeddings on ~20% of calls (avg 512 tokens).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for single-shot generation where possible.

Ask for: a rough sizing recommendation (GPU type + count), any warm-pool or batching guidance, and a preliminary quote we can share with procurement. Also please confirm if H100 vs A100 makes a material difference for our mix.

I'll loop in procurement after your estimate — they want the security checklist and an indicative quote.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Green
Head of AI, Fintech Labs
alex.green@fintechlabs.com
https://fintechlabs.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Alex — appreciate the clear summary. Quick clarifying q's before I finalize a sizing sketch with Marissa (solutions engineering):

1) Is 250 TPS your expected peak burst target (i.e., short spikes), or sustained for multiple minutes?
2) Are the embeddings served from the same endpoints or a separate embeddings service?
3) Any hard constraints on cost vs latency we should prioritize (e.g., absolute max monthly spend)?

Prelim thoughts (very rough):
- With your token mix (40/160 gen) and ~20% embeddings, 250 TPS peak with 50 concurrency typically maps to 3-5 A100-80GB GPUs or 3-4 H100-80GB GPUs depending on model and quantization.
- H100 tends to give ~15-25% better throughput for long-context generative workloads and lower latency at high concurrency, but A100 can be more cost-efficient if you can tolerate slightly higher p95.
- We'll leverage continuous batching + KV prefix caching to reduce per-token cost for repeated prompts; warm pool of spare instances recommended for bursty patterns.

I attached a short estimate (Redwood_dedicated_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf) with a couple of node-count scenarios and per-token cost assumptions. Marissa can run a tighter sizing once we confirm the burst duration and whether embeddings are separate.

Next steps: if it works for you, let's schedule a 30–45m sizing call with Marissa to lock down the node type and get a formal quote. I'll include procurement contacts in the next thread once you confirm.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Aditya — thanks. Answers below:

1) Peak bursts are short (1–3 minutes), but we see multiple bursts per hour during business hours. Sustained baseline ~120 TPS.
2) Embeddings run on a separate endpoint/service but will share the same Dedicated pool for now.
3) Cost sensitivity: prefer minimizing monthly spend but not at the expense of missing the latency SLO. We can trade a small delta in cost for consistent p95 < 400ms.

Numbers for sizing:
- Peak TPS (burst): 250 TPS
- Sustained TPS: 120 TPS
- Concurrency target: 50
- Prompt tokens: 40 avg
- Generated tokens: 160 avg
- Embeddings: ~20% of calls at avg 512 tokens

Attaching our security checklist so you can see the procurement asks (Fintech_security_checklist.pdf). Procurement: please let us know any additional docs needed to move to SOW/PO.

Happy to do a sizing call this week.

—Alex
Alex Green
Head of AI, Fintech Labs

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Alex / procurement team — thanks for the fast reply and the checklist. Based on the details you sent, here's a recommended starting configuration and next steps: 

Recommended "starter" configurations (conservative sizing with room to tune):
- Option A (performance-first): 4 x NVIDIA H100-80GB GPUs (serving runtime tuned for 1.5–2x batching). Expected to comfortably cover 250 TPS bursts with p95 ~300–380ms for your token mix and concurrency ~50. Better headroom for longer generations.
- Option B (cost-balanced): 5 x NVIDIA A100-80GB GPUs. Slightly higher p95 (~350–420ms) on peak but lower monthly cost. Good if you want to optimize for spend and are okay with slightly less headroom.

Operational notes:
- We'll enable continuous batching with a warm pool of +1 spare machine to smooth spikes.
- Embeddings in the same pool will be routed with priority rules to prevent embedding jobs from saturating generation capacity; we can put embeddings on lower-priority nodes if desired.
- We'll use KV prefix caching for repeated prompts to cut token costs on common requests.

Attachments / next docs: I've attached a preliminary quote (RDW-2026-3749-quote.docx) and the estimate PDF I shared earlier. Marissa can run a tighter model-level capacity plan (model variants, quantization options) in the sizing call.

Proposed next steps: 
1) 30–45m sizing + procurement sync with Marissa (solutions engineering) this week — calendar: https://calendly.com/marissa/redwood-sizing-call
2) We finalize node type (H100 vs A100) and model quantization choices
3) Redwood generates formal SOW/quote and we loop in procurement for PO

Let me know two times that work this week and I will put the invite on the calendar.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
